title: Customer Data Classification
text: Customer personal data must be classified before ingestion into any AI workflow. Sensitive customer records require restricted access, purpose limitation, retention controls and documented approval. Never index raw personal identifiers into a shared retrieval collection.

title: Knowledge Assistant Architecture
text: The enterprise knowledge assistant uses an API gateway, identity validation, document ingestion, chunking, an indexed retrieval layer, an evidence gate and an answer service. Requests without supporting evidence must abstain and offer escalation. Every response stores trace identifiers and cited source identifiers.

title: Incident Response Escalation
text: Security incidents involving exposed credentials must be escalated immediately to the security operations team. Contain affected access, preserve evidence, document the timeline and assign an incident owner before remediation. Notify the service owner of customer impact.

title: Production Readiness Criteria
text: Production release requires documented threat modeling, a tested rollback plan, owner approval, baseline evaluation results and alerting for failures. Evaluation must include grounded answer rate, abstention correctness, response latency and operational cost. A failed safety gate blocks release.

title: Retrieval Evaluation Standard
text: Retrieval quality is assessed using a versioned question set with expected source documents. Measure citation precision, answer support, correct abstention and retrieval relevance. Run regression evaluations after changing chunking, embeddings, prompts or source documents.

title: Identity and Access Controls
text: Employees authenticate through the corporate identity provider with multifactor authentication. Retrieval results must be filtered by document access permissions before being presented to the answer service. Service accounts use least privilege and short-lived credentials.

title: Cost and Latency Budget
text: Model operating cost depends on request volume, input tokens, output tokens and the selected model rates. Monitor p95 latency, cache hit rate, retrieval time and cost per successful answer. Set budget alerts and evaluate smaller models for low-risk tasks.

title: Human Approval for Actions
text: An AI agent may draft changes but cannot execute high-impact actions without explicit human approval. Tools are allowlisted, inputs are validated, and each proposed action records the requester, justification and decision. Denied actions are logged for review.

title: Hybrid Cloud Integration
text: The integration pattern uses private network connectivity, a managed secrets store, role-based service identities and an event queue for asynchronous jobs. Legacy enterprise systems are accessed through narrowly scoped adapters with retries, timeouts and circuit breakers.

title: Supplier and Ownership Model
text: The client owns business decisions and data access policy. The delivery team owns implementation and technical documentation. The managed platform provider owns infrastructure incidents under an agreed service-level agreement. Changes require an accountable owner and recorded acceptance criteria.
